title: His wealth and sons made him arrogant, not grateful.
subtitle: When blessings become a reason to look down

row.title: I have, so I am above
I have, so I give thanks

then: Ibn Kathir says this is how he responded to {reward}the favors of wealth and children Allah gave him{/reward}: by {trap}disbelieving in Allah's verses and turning away.{/trap} The Quran describes a similar man elsewhere, given plenty and still wanting more.
now: The raise comes through. The kids get into good schools. The house gets bigger. {trap}Slowly you start listening less, to people and to reminders.{/trap} {idea}Every blessing is a test of which way it pushes you.{/idea}
old: I have done well, so I must be on the right track.
new: Wealth and family are gifts that test me, not proof that I am right.
try: List three blessings you have now that you did not have five years ago. Thank Allah for each by name.

title: Old stories, he says, to dodge what the verses ask.
subtitle: Dismissing a reminder instead of hearing it

row.title: legends of old
sub: a lie copied from the ancients

then: When the verses were recited to this man of Makkah, he waved them off. Ibn Kathir says he claimed {trap}they were a lie taken from the tales of the ancients.{/trap} It was easier than facing what they said about his {trap}wealth and pride.{/trap}
now: A friend sends a reminder in the group chat and you think, here we go again. A khutbah touches something real and you file it under old fashioned. {trap}Dismissing is faster than listening.{/trap} {idea}What if it was meant for you?{/idea}
old: I have heard this all before. It does not apply to me.
new: A reminder I am quick to dismiss may be the one I most need.
try: Next time a reminder annoys you, ask: what exactly is it asking me to change?

title: The proud nose will carry a mark everyone can see.
subtitle: What he hid will be made plain

row.title: branded
sub: his matter made clear to all

row.title: it will be made plain
sub: like a mark on the face

then: Ibn Jarir said it means Allah {idea}will make his matter clear so people know him{/idea}, like a brand on an animal. Others said it is {trap}the mark of the people of the Fire on the Day of Judgment.{/trap} The proud face is the very place that is marked.
now: You keep a polished image online. The perfect posts, the careful replies. Behind it, the things nobody sees. {trap}Hidden things have a way of showing.{/trap} {idea}Better to fix them now than have them made plain later.{/idea}
old: As long as nobody sees it, it does not matter.
new: What I hide is not hidden from Allah, and one day it will show.
try: Pick one private habit you would be ashamed to have shown. Take one step away from it today.

title: Makkah was tested like the owners of the garden.
subtitle: A parable about a blessing and a choice

row.title: tested
sub: what will you do with it?

row.title: a test
sub: what you do with it counts

then: Ibn Kathir says this parable is about {reward}the great mercy of sending Muhammad ﷺ{/reward} to Quraysh, who met it with denial. The garden owners {trap}swore at night to harvest early{/trap} so the poor would not know.
now: Your bonus lands. A new job, a healthy baby, a good harvest of any kind. {idea}Each one is a garden and a test.{/idea} The question is what you plan at night about who gets a share.
old: Good things happen to me. Tests are the bad things.
new: Blessings are tests too. What I do with them is the answer.
try: Look at your latest blessing and decide one share of it to give away this week.

title: They made plans without saying if Allah wills.
subtitle: The missing words in a confident plan
then: The owners swore to harvest in the morning, {trap}without saying if Allah wills.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says that because of this, {idea}Allah broke their vow.{/idea} They spoke as if tomorrow was already theirs.
now: I will finish the project by Friday. We are moving next month. He will definitely get the job. {trap}You say it like tomorrow is in your pocket.{/trap} {idea}Two words put it back in Allah's hands.{/idea}
old: If I plan well enough, it will happen.
new: I plan, but tomorrow belongs to Allah. Insha'Allah is honesty, not a habit.
try: Say insha'Allah, meaning it, every time you speak about tomorrow today.

title: While they slept, their garden was already gone.
subtitle: What happens while you are confident and asleep
then: They went to bed with their plan settled. Ibn Kathir says the garden {trap}was struck by a heavenly destruction{/trap} that night. {idea}They were asleep and knew nothing of it.{/idea}
now: You fall asleep with your phone on the charger, calendar full, plans set for the morning. {idea}So much changes in the world while you sleep.{/idea} Your plans were never fully in your hands.
old: My plans are secure because I made them carefully.
new: Everything I count on is held by Allah, even while I sleep.
try: Tonight, before sleeping, hand tomorrow to Allah in your own words.

title: By morning the garden looked like it had been reaped.
subtitle: From full to nothing in one night
then: Ibn Abbas said the garden became {trap}like the dark night.{/trap} Ath-Thawri and As-Suddi said it was {trap}like a crop harvested, withered and dry.{/trap} What took seasons to grow was gone by dawn.
now: A market crashes. A diagnosis arrives. A message ends a friendship. {trap}What took years can change in a morning.{/trap} {idea}It is a reason to hold blessings with open hands and grateful hearts.{/idea}
old: What I have built will always be there.
new: Anything I have can change in a night, so I should thank and share while I can.
try: Thank Allah today for one thing you would hate to lose, and use it well.

title: At dawn they called each other, still sure of their plan.
subtitle: Waking up excited about something already gone
then: Ibn Kathir says in the early morning {idea}they called each other to go together{/idea} and pick the harvest. They had no idea {trap}what had happened in the night.{/trap}
now: You wake up and message the team: let us go, big day. Full of energy for the plan. {trap}We are often most sure right before the surprise.{/trap} {idea}Humility in the morning costs nothing.{/idea}
old: I know exactly how today will go.
new: I start each day not knowing what Allah has already decreed for it.
try: Start tomorrow's first message or call with bismillah, said with attention.

title: Go early, they said, before anyone else can come.
subtitle: Rushing so no one else gets a share
then: Go early to your crop, they said. Ibn Kathir explains the whole plan was to pick the fruit {trap}so the poor and the beggars would not know{/trap}, and they could {trap}keep it all and give none in charity.{/trap}
now: You order delivery after the kids are asleep so you do not have to share. You leave the office quietly so no one asks for a lift. {trap}Small timing tricks to avoid giving.{/trap} {idea}The plan reveals the heart.{/idea}
old: Being early and smart is just good planning.
new: Planning to avoid giving is not smart. It is the garden owners' mistake.
try: Notice one small way you dodge sharing. Do the opposite once today.

title: They whispered, but Allah heard every word.
subtitle: Secret plans are not secret from Allah

row.title: Allah
sub: and He told us what they said

then: They walked and spoke in low voices so no one could hear. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}Allah, the Knower of secrets and private talks{/idea}, then revealed exactly what they whispered. {trap}The hidden plan was told in the Quran for all time.{/trap}
now: The private chat. The DM you would never want screenshotted. The plan you only say behind a closed door. {idea}Allah hears it all, the same as if it were shouted.{/idea}
old: What I say in private stays private.
new: Allah hears my whispers as clearly as my words in public.
try: Read back your last private conversation. Would you be comfortable with Allah reading it? He has.

title: Not one poor person gets in today.
subtitle: The exact words that cost them everything
then: Ibn Kathir reports one account that their father used to {reward}give the excess of the harvest in charity.{/reward} When he died, the sons said he was foolish, and if they {trap}kept the poor out, they would have more.{/trap}
now: Your parents always had an extra plate for whoever dropped by. Now you count every cost and think that was naive. {trap}Closing the door feels like good management.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the generous habit was the blessing itself.{/idea}
old: If I stop giving, I will have more for myself.
new: Shutting out the poor does not protect my wealth. It can be what removes it.
try: Keep one good habit of giving you inherited from a parent or elder, or restart it this week.

title: They marched out sure they had full control.
subtitle: Confidence in your own power
then: Ibn Kathir says they went {trap}with strength and power{/trap}, and they {trap}thought they had the power to do what they wanted.{/trap} They felt fully in charge of something that was no longer there.
now: You walk into the meeting with the deal already signed in your head. You budget the money before the contract arrives. {trap}Confidence can slide into thinking you control the outcome.{/trap} {idea}Prepare, then hold the result loosely.{/idea}
old: I have the skill and resources, so I control the result.
new: My effort is mine. The outcome is Allah's.
try: Before your next big task, pause and say: Allah, I did my part, the result is Yours.

title: This cannot be our garden. We must be lost.
subtitle: The first reaction is denial
then: When they arrived, the garden had gone {trap}from luster and abundance to black and empty.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said they first thought {idea}they had taken the wrong path.{/idea} It could not be theirs.
now: The bank balance. The test result. The message from the school. Your first thought: that cannot be right, there must be a mistake. {idea}Denial is the first step before facing what happened.{/idea}
old: This cannot be happening to me.
new: When loss comes, the first honest step is to admit it is real.
try: Name one hard thing you have been refusing to look at. Look at it, with a du'a.
